$comment: Customization-only application catalog. Every app must have purpose='customization' and categories drawn from allowedCategories; apps.js rejects anything else. 'projects' are the owner's own apps, listed for convenience and exempt from that rule (they are labelled as such in the UI). Install commands are shown and run only after the user asks.

apps.name: GNOME Tweaks
apps.description: The official knob panel for GNOME: titlebar buttons, fonts, startup apps, top bar, workspaces and extension switches.
apps.note: Everything it changes is a gsettings key, so Twiking mods coexist — a value set here after a mod was enabled wins until you re-apply the mod.

apps.name: Zorin Appearance
apps.description: Zorin's own layout and colour switcher: desktop layouts, accent colours, theme variants and taskbar behaviour.
apps.note: Switching layout here rewrites several of the same gsettings keys the Window Buttons, Dock & Panel and Workspaces mods use.

apps.name: Extension Manager
apps.description: Browse, install and update GNOME Shell extensions — the biggest source of shell-level customisation on GNOME.
apps.note: Extensions run inside gnome-shell. A broken one can blank the shell; keep a terminal or TTY handy the first time you install one.

apps.name: dconf Editor
apps.description: Raw browser for every GSettings key on the system, with descriptions — the source of truth behind every Twiking settings mod.
apps.note: No undo and no explanation of consequences. Great for exploring, risky for changing.

apps.name: GNOME Shell Extensions (pack)
apps.description: The classic official extension set: app menu, window list, workspace indicator, auto-move windows, places menu and more.
apps.note: Installing adds the extension files; enable them individually in Extensions or Extension Manager.

apps.name: AppIndicator Support
apps.description: Brings legacy tray icons into the GNOME top bar — needed by Discord, Steam, Dropbox and many others.
apps.note: Log out and back in after installing so the shell picks it up.

apps.name: Ubuntu Dock (Dash to Dock)
apps.description: The configurable application dock behind Ubuntu's launcher: position, size, autohide and click behaviour.
apps.note: On Zorin this overlaps with the built-in taskbar; enable one dock, not both.

apps.name: Kvantum
apps.description: SVG-based Qt theme engine with a large style library; makes Qt apps match a GTK desktop.
apps.note: Requires QT_STYLE_OVERRIDE=kvantum — the Qt App Styling mod does that for you.

apps.name: Qt6 Configuration Tool
apps.description: Configures fonts, icons, palette and style for Qt 6 applications.
apps.note: Sets QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct via the Qt App Styling mod.

apps.name: Adwaita for Qt
apps.description: Adwaita look-alike style for Qt 5 applications, so they stop looking out of place next to GTK apps.
apps.note: Pair with the Qt App Styling mod set to the GTK3 bridge.

apps.name: Gradience
apps.description: Generates complete libadwaita colour schemes from a few colours, including shell theming.
apps.note: Writes user CSS and theme colours; enable either this or Twiking's GTK CSS mods, not both.

apps.name: Papirus Icons
apps.description: The most popular icon theme family on Linux, with colour variants for folders and a matching cursor set.
apps.note: Pure data — installing adds no process and no risk.

apps.name: Numix Circle Icons
apps.description: Flat, circular icon theme that covers a very large number of applications.
apps.note: Switch to it with the Icon Theme mod.

apps.name: elementary Icons
apps.description: Clean, rounded icon set from elementary OS — a gentle alternative to Papirus.
apps.note: Includes cursor themes as well.

apps.name: Humanity Icons
apps.description: The classic Ubuntu icon set, still useful for older apps that need full coverage.
apps.note: Best paired with the Yaru or Arc GTK themes.

apps.name: Yaru Icons
apps.description: Ubuntu's modern icon theme, with light, dark and accent-coloured folder variants.
apps.note: Yaru GTK and Yaru icons are separate packages; install both for a consistent look.

apps.name: Yaru GTK Theme
apps.description: Ubuntu's GTK theme — warm greys, an orange accent and a matching dark variant.
apps.note: Pick it in the GTK Theme mod after installing.

apps.name: Arc Theme
apps.description: The long-running flat theme with transparent elements; still one of the most downloaded GTK themes.
apps.note: Includes GNOME Shell and GTK2/3/4 variants.

apps.name: Numix GTK Theme
apps.description: Flat, colourful GTK theme designed to pair with the Numix icon set.
apps.note: GTK3 era; modern libadwaita apps will only partly follow it.

apps.name: Breeze Cursors
apps.description: KDE's crisp, high-contrast cursor set — widely considered the easiest to track on screen.
apps.note: Switch to it with the Cursor Theme mod.

apps.name: Inter Font
apps.description: The screen-first sans-serif GNOME and Zorin already lean on; install it everywhere it is missing.
apps.note: Pick it in the System Fonts mod.

apps.name: JetBrains Mono
apps.description: A coding font with tall x-height and clear punctuation — comfortable for terminals.
apps.note: Set it as the monospace font in System Fonts.

apps.name: Fira Code
apps.description: Monospace font with programming ligatures (=>, !=, >=) for terminals and editors.
apps.note: Ligatures only appear in apps that opt in, such as most code editors.

apps.name: Cantarell Font
apps.description: GNOME's own UI typeface — the safest choice for a consistent GNOME look.
apps.note: Already present on most GNOME installs; this guarantees the latest cut.

apps.name: Noto Color Emoji
apps.description: Full-colour emoji font so chat, browsers and terminals stop showing empty boxes.
apps.note: Some apps cache their emoji font until restarted.

apps.name: Font Manager
apps.description: Preview, install and compare fonts, and see exactly how a family renders at different sizes.
apps.note: Installed fonts appear in the System Fonts mod after a rescan.

apps.name: GNOME Backgrounds
apps.description: The official GNOME wallpaper collection, including the light/dark companion pairs.
apps.note: Pairs well with the Wallpaper mod's light/dark image options.

apps.name: Ubuntu Wallpapers
apps.description: Every Ubuntu release wallpaper plus the mascot artwork, installed system-wide.
apps.note: A few hundred MB of images; remove with apt if you change your mind.

apps.name: Variety
apps.description: Rotates wallpapers from local folders or online sources on a schedule, with quotes and effects.
apps.note: Runs a background daemon; stop it from its own tray menu.

apps.name: Nitrogen
apps.description: Fast wallpaper setter for lightweight desktops and multi-monitor setups.
apps.note: Only needed on desktops that don't manage their own wallpaper.

apps.name: Plank
apps.description: Minimal, themeable application dock for any desktop.
apps.note: Adds a dock without touching GNOME's own layout.

apps.name: Cairo-Dock
apps.description: Heavily animated dock with 3D effects, applets and themes — the opposite of minimal.
apps.note: Best on X11; under Wayland some effects are unavailable.

apps.name: Latte Dock
apps.description: KDE's flexible dock and panel system, with parabolic zoom and per-activity layouts.
apps.note: Aimed at Plasma; on GNOME it can only run as a standalone dock.

apps.name: Picom Compositor
apps.description: Standalone compositor offering shadows, blur, fading and transparency for X11 desktops.
apps.note: X11 only — it has no effect under a Wayland session like this one.

apps.name: Conky
apps.description: Classic always-on desktop widget system: CPU, memory, weather, media, anything scriptable.
apps.note: Conky configs are plain text in ~/.config/conky; a bad one is fixed by editing the file.

apps.name: LXAppearance
apps.description: Lightweight GTK theme, icon and cursor switcher that works outside GNOME too.
apps.note: Writes GTK settings.ini; GNOME ignores parts of that, so prefer Zorin Appearance here.

projects.name: Windows 11 File Explorer for Linux
projects.description: Pixel-faithful Electron recreation of File Explorer: tabs, Fluent design, Quick access, This PC, Recycle Bin, .deb packaging.
projects.note: Your project — listed for quick access. Not part of the customization-only catalogue.

projects.name: Windows 11 Task Manager for Linux
projects.description: Task Manager clone reading live data from /proc: processes, CPU/memory/disk/network graphs, services, startup apps.
projects.note: Your project — listed for quick access. Launching uses its installed .desktop entry; the source is on GitHub.
